events.title: The apparition of St. Michael at Monte Gargano
events.shortBlurb: By ancient tradition the Archangel Michael appeared on Monte Gargano, giving rise to one of the great western shrines…
body: According to the ancient Liber de Apparitione, about the year 490 a rich man of Siponto, hunting a stray bull, found it kneeling at the mouth of a cave on Monte Gargano in Apulia, and the arrow he loosed at the beast turned back upon the archer. After three days of fasting, Michael the Archangel appeared to Lawrence, bishop of Siponto, and claimed the cave for his own.

The grotto was never dedicated by human hands, the Archangel declaring that he had consecrated it himself; it became the sanctuary of Monte Sant'Angelo, the oldest shrine of the Archangel in the West. The feast of 8 May was joined to the memory of a victory over the pagan besiegers of Siponto, won through his aid.

From Gargano the veneration of Michael spread through the Latin Church, and for fifteen centuries the mountain shrine drew pilgrims of every age, Lombard kings, Norman knights, popes, and crusaders who made it a station on the road to the Holy Land.
